newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UK's Cook hails positive visit to Russia.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cook hails positive visit to Russia.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook on Tuesday wrapped up two days of talks in Moscow hailing concrete progress in cooperation against crime and the prospect of boosting trade and economic links.

Cook said his visit had been overwhelmingly positive and shown that Britain was highly regarded in Moscow, especially as the new Labour government was adopting a more positive attitude towards Europe.
"We're no longer seen as an odd one out. We're seen as one of the senior players," Cook told reporters.
"I think now there's a willingness to recognise that we also have a relationship with Europe that is worth courting," he said.
Cook was the first cabinet minister to visit Russia since Tony Blair's Labour party ousted the Conservatives after 18 years of power in a landslide election victory on May 1.

Blair himself is due to visit Moscow later in the year and Cook said his talks with Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov had successfully paved the way for the prime minister's visit.
Earlier, Cook finalised an agreement with General Vladimir Kolesnikov, Russia's deputy interior minister, to step up cooperation in the fight against crime and drugs trafficking.
Under the pact, to be signed by Blair, the law enforcement agencies of Britain and Russia will exchange information, documents and materials and share experience and expertise.
"We need to cooperate as closely as the criminals do," Cook said.
He said he was particularly impressed by Nemtsov, describing him as "breathtakingly businesslike"" and a "can-do" politician.
